tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, with Wealthsimple and KOHO already announcing adoption, so instant payments become a baseline expectation. BMO is also pushing AI into servicing, and Venmo's bill-splitting and stablecoin moves are raising the bar on peer-to-peer and payments features.
themes: AI assistants in servicing and business apps
Stablecoins and tokenized assets moving into mainstream finance
Premium card and sign-up bonus competition

highlights.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail launched, and Wealthsimple and KOHO are already announcing adoption; Interac issued a statement on the launch
highlights.why: Instant payments are now live in Canada and direct competitor Wealthsimple is publicly claiming a place on the rail. Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline and customer messaging, since faster-payments expectations will reset quickly.

highlights.headline: BMO launched AI Agent Assist for its credit card contact centre (Nov 6)
highlights.why: A big-bank peer is using generative AI to speed up service resolution. Simplii's servicing and contact-centre teams should compare it against their own AI roadmap, though this is an agent-assist tool rather than a customer-facing assistant.

highlights.headline: Venmo added receipt scanning to split bills by item, with wide coverage from Engadget, Fast Company and USA Today
highlights.why: Itemized bill splitting is becoming standard in peer-to-peer payments. Simplii could consider a similar feature alongside Interac e-Transfer and RTR.

highlights.headline: PNC is launching incoming stablecoin payments for corporate clients with Coinbase, and Coinbase received a US national trust charter
highlights.why: Stablecoin and crypto activity is moving into regulated banking. It is mostly a corporate and US story for now, but it signals where payments and custody are heading, so Simplii should keep it on its watchlist.
